.. py:function:: hipsparseXcsrsort(handle, m, n, nnz, descrA, csrRowPtr, csrColInd, P, pBuffer)

   Sort a sparse CSR matrix.

   ``hipsparseXcsrsort`` sorts a matrix in CSR format. The sorted permutation vector
   ``P`` can be used to obtain the sorted ``csrVal`` array. In this case, ``P`` must be
   initialized as the identity permutation. See ``hipsparseCreateIdentityPermutation`` (). To
   apply the permutation vector to the CSR values, see ``hipsparseSgthr`` 
   "hipsparseXgthr()".

   ``hipsparseXcsrsort`` requires extra temporary storage buffer that must be allocated by
   the user. The storage buffer size can be determined by hipsparseXcsrsort_bufferSizeExt().

   Note:
       ``P`` can be ``NULL`` if a sorted permutation vector is not required.

   Note:
       This function is non-blocking and executed asynchronously with respect to the host.
       It can return before the actual computation has finished.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the sparse CSR matrix.

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the sparse CSR matrix.

       nnz (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of non-zero entries of the sparse CSR matrix.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           descriptor of the sparse CSR matrix. Currently, only
           ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` is supported.

       csrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           sparse CSR matrix.

       csrColInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *INOUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the column indices of the sparse
           CSR matrix.

       P (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *INOUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` integers containing the unsorted map indices. Can be
           ``NULL.``

       pBuffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user. The size is returned by
           ``hipsparseXcsrsort_bufferSizeExt`` ().

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``m,`` ``n,`` ``nnz,`` ``descrA,`` ``csrRowPtr,``
                 ``csrColInd,`` or ``pBuffer`` pointer is invalid.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`: an internal error occurred.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`: ``hipsparseMatrixType_t`` != ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` .

.. py:function:: hipsparseSdense2csc(handle, m, n, descr, A, ld, nnzPerColumn, cscVal, cscRowInd, cscColPtr)

   ``hipsparseXdense2csc`` functions convert the matrix ``A`` in dense format into a sparse matrix in CSC format.

   Given a dense, column-ordered, matrix ``A`` with leading dimension ``ld,`` where ``ld>=m,``
   ``hipsparseXdense2csc`` converts the matrix to a sparse CSC format matrix.
   All the parameters are assumed to have been preallocated by the user and the arrays
   are filled in based on number of non-zeros per row, which can be pre-computed with
   ``hipsparseSnnz`` . Users can set the desired index base in the output CSC
   matrix by setting it in the ``hipsparseMatDescr_t`` . See ``hipsparseSetMatIndexBase`` ().

   As an example, if using index base zero (that is, the default) and the dense
   matrix:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\
      3 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\
      5 & 0 & 6 & 7
      \end{bmatrix}

   where the ``A`` values have column ordering with leading dimension ``ld=m:``

   .. math::

      \text{A} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 5 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 & 2 & 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \\

   the conversion results in the CSC arrays:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{cscRowInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{cscColPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{cscVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 5 & 4 & 6 & 2 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \end{align}

   Note:
       This function is executed asynchronously with respect to the host and can return control to the
       application on the host before the entire result is ready.

   Deprecated:
       This function is deprecated when using the CUDA backend (CUDA 11.0+) and will be
       removed in CUDA 12.0. This deprecation does not apply to the ROCm backend.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       descr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.`` The supported matrix type is  ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` and
           any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``ld,`` ``n).``

       ld (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of dense array ``A.`` Must be at least ``m.``

       nnzPerColumn (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of size ``n`` containing the number of non-zero elements per column.

       cscVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of nnz ( = ``cscColPtr[n]`` - ``cscColPtr[0]`` ) nonzero elements of matrix ``A.``

       cscRowInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           integer array of nnz ( = ``cscColPtr[n]`` - ``cscColPtr[0]`` ) column indices of the non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

       cscColPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           integer array of ``n+1`` elements that contains the start of every column and the end of the last column plus one.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`: ``handle`` is not initialized.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``descr,`` ``A,`` ``nnzPerColumn,`` ``cscVal,``
                 ``cscColPtr,`` or ``cscRowInd`` is nullptr, ``m`` or ``n`` is negative, or ``ld`` is invalid.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseSdense2csc(hipsparseHandle_t handle, int m, int n, const hipsparseMatDescr_t descr, const float * A, int ld, const int * nnzPerColumn, float * cscVal, int * cscRowInd, int * cscColPtr)

   Given a dense, column-ordered, matrix ``A`` with leading dimension ``ld,`` where ``ld>=m,``

.. py:function:: hipsparseSgebsr2csr(handle, dirA, mb, nb, descrA, bsrValA, bsrRowPtrA, bsrColIndA, rowBlockDim, colBlockDim, descrC, csrValC, csrRowPtrC, csrColIndC)

   Convert a sparse GEBSR matrix into a sparse CSR matrix.

   ``hipsparseXgebsr2csr`` converts a GEBSR matrix into a CSR matrix. It is assumed
   that ``csrValC,`` ``csrColIndC,`` and ``csrRowPtrC`` are already allocated prior to
   calling ``hipsparseXgebsr2csr.`` Allocation size for ``csrRowPtrC`` equals
   ``m+1`` where:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{m} &= \text{mb * rowBlockDim} \\
      \text{n} &= \text{nb * colBlockDim}
      \end{align}

   Allocation size for ``csrValC`` and ``csrColIndC`` is computed by the the number of blocks in the GEBSR
   matrix, ``nnzb,`` multiplied by the product of the block dimensions, that is, ``nnz=nnzb*rocBlockDim*colBlockDim.``

   For example, given the GEBSR matrix:

   .. math::

       \left[
        \begin{array}{c | c | c}
          \begin{array}{c c}
           6 & 2 \\
           1 & 4 \\
           5 & 4
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 3 \\
           5 & 0 \\
           0 & 7
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           3 & 0 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 7
          \end{array} &

.. py:function:: hipsparseSgebsr2gebsc(handle, mb, nb, nnzb, bsrVal, bsrRowPtr, bsrColInd, rowBlockDim, colBlockDim, bscVal, bscRowInd, bscColPtr, copyValues, idxBase, temp_buffer)

   Convert a sparse GEBSR matrix into a sparse GEBSC matrix

   ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc`` converts a GEBSR matrix into a GEBSC matrix. ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc``
   can also be used to convert a GEBSC matrix into a GEBSR matrix. ``copyValues`` decides
   whether ``bscVal`` is being filled during conversion (``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_NUMERIC`` )
   or not (``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_SYMBOLIC`` ).

   ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc`` requires extra temporary storage buffer that has to be allocated
   by the user. Storage buffer size can be determined by ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize`` 
   "hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize()".

   For example, given the GEBSR matrix:

   .. math::

       \left[
        \begin{array}{c | c}
          \begin{array}{c c}
           1 & 2 \\
           3 & 4 \\
           6 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 2 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c}
           5 & 0 \\
           1 & 2 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           6 & 7 \\
           3 & 4 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} \\
       \end{array}
      \right]

   represented with the arrays:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{bsrRowPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bsrColInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bsrVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 3 & 4 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
      \end{align}

   this function converts the matrix to GEBSC format:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{bscRowInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bscColPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bscVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 3 & 4 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
      \end{align}

   Note:
       The resulting matrix can also be seen as the transpose of the input matrix.

   Note:
       This function is non-blocking and executed asynchronously with respect to the host.
       It can return before the actual computation has finished.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       mb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       nb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       nnzb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of non-zero entries of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzb`` * ``rowBlockDim`` * ``colBlockDim``  elements of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrColInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the column indices of the sparse
           general BSR matrix.

       rowBlockDim (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           row size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix.

       colBlockDim (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           col size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bscVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements of the sparse BSC matrix.

       bscRowInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the row indices of the sparse BSC
           matrix.

       bscColPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``n+1`` elements that point to the start of every column of the
           sparse BSC matrix.

       copyValues (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseAction_t`) -- *IN*:
           ``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_SYMBOLIC`` or ``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_NUMERIC`` .

       idxBase (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseIndexBase_t`) -- *IN*:
           ``HIPSPARSE_INDEX_BASE_ZERO`` or ``HIPSPARSE_INDEX_BASE_ONE`` .

       temp_buffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user. The size is returned by
           ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize`` .

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``mb,`` ``nb,`` ``nnzb,`` ``bsrVal,``

               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_ARCH_MISMATCH`: the device is not supported.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`: an internal error occurred.

.. py:function:: hipsparseZgebsr2gebsc(handle, mb, nb, nnzb, bsrVal, bsrRowPtr, bsrColInd, rowBlockDim, colBlockDim, bscVal, bscRowInd, bscColPtr, copyValues, idxBase, temp_buffer)

   Convert a sparse GEBSR matrix into a sparse GEBSC matrix

   ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc`` converts a GEBSR matrix into a GEBSC matrix. ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc``
   can also be used to convert a GEBSC matrix into a GEBSR matrix. ``copyValues`` decides
   whether ``bscVal`` is being filled during conversion (``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_NUMERIC`` )
   or not (``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_SYMBOLIC`` ).

   ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc`` requires extra temporary storage buffer that has to be allocated
   by the user. Storage buffer size can be determined by ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize`` 
   "hipsparseXgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize()".

   For example, given the GEBSR matrix:

   .. math::

       \left[
        \begin{array}{c | c}
          \begin{array}{c c}
           1 & 2 \\
           3 & 4 \\
           6 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 2 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c}
           5 & 0 \\
           1 & 2 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           6 & 7 \\
           3 & 4 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} \\
       \end{array}
      \right]

   represented with the arrays:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{bsrRowPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bsrColInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bsrVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 3 & 4 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
      \end{align}

   this function converts the matrix to GEBSC format:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{bscRowInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bscColPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{bscVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 3 & 4 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
      \end{align}

   Note:
       The resulting matrix can also be seen as the transpose of the input matrix.

   Note:
       This function is non-blocking and executed asynchronously with respect to the host.
       It can return before the actual computation has finished.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       mb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       nb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       nnzb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of non-zero entries of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzb`` * ``rowBlockDim`` * ``colBlockDim``  elements of the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           sparse general BSR matrix.

       bsrColInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the column indices of the sparse
           general BSR matrix.

       rowBlockDim (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           row size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix.

       colBlockDim (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           col size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix.

       bscVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements of the sparse BSC matrix.

       bscRowInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the row indices of the sparse BSC
           matrix.

       bscColPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of ``n+1`` elements that point to the start of every column of the
           sparse BSC matrix.

       copyValues (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseAction_t`) -- *IN*:
           ``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_SYMBOLIC`` or ``HIPSPARSE_ACTION_NUMERIC`` .

       idxBase (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseIndexBase_t`) -- *IN*:
           ``HIPSPARSE_INDEX_BASE_ZERO`` or ``HIPSPARSE_INDEX_BASE_ONE`` .

       temp_buffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user. The size is returned by
           ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsc_bufferSize`` .

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``mb,`` ``nb,`` ``nnzb,`` ``bsrVal,``
                 ``bsrRowPtr,`` ``bsrColInd,`` ``bscVal,`` ``bscRowInd,`` ``bscColPtr,`` or
                 ``temp_buffer`` pointer is invalid.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_ARCH_MISMATCH`: the device is not supported.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`: an internal error occurred.

.. py:function:: hipsparseXgebsr2gebsrNnz(handle, dirA, mb, nb, nnzb, descrA, bsrRowPtrA, bsrColIndA, rowBlockDimA, colBlockDimA, descrC, bsrRowPtrC, rowBlockDimC, colBlockDimC, nnzTotalDevHostPtr, buffer)

   This function is used when converting a GEBSR sparse matrix :math:`A` to another GEBSR sparse matrix :math:`C`.
   Specifically, this function determines the number of non-zero blocks that will exist in :math:`C` (stored using either a host
   or device pointer) and computes the row pointer array for :math:`C`.

   The routine supports asynchronous execution.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       dirA (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseDirection_t`) -- *IN*:
           the storage format of the blocks, ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_ROW`` or ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_COLUMN`` .

       mb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of block rows of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       nb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of block columns of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       nnzb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of blocks in the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:

   The conversion uses three steps. First, the user calls ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize`` 
   "hipsparseXgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize()" to determine the size of the required temporary storage buffer.
   The user then allocates this buffer. Secondly, the user then allocates ``mbC+1`` integers for the row
   pointer array for :math:`C` where:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{mbC} &= \text{(m - 1) / rowBlockDimC + 1} \\
      \text{nbC} &= \text{(n - 1) / colBlockDimC + 1}
      \end{align}

   The user then calls hipsparseXgebsr2gebsrNnz() to fill in the row pointer array for :math:`C` ( ``bsrRowPtrC`` ) and
   determine the number of non-zero blocks that will exist in :math:`C`. Finally, the user allocates space for the column
   indices array of :math:`C` to have ``nnzbC`` elements and space for the values array of :math:`C` to have
   ``nnzbC*rowBlockDimC*colBlockDimC`` and then calls ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsr`` to complete the conversion.

   It could be the case that ``rowBlockDimC`` does not divide evenly into ``m`` or ``colBlockDim`` does not divide evenly
   into ``n.`` In these cases, the GEBSR matrix is expanded in size to fit full GEBSR blocks. For example, if
   the original GEBSR matrix A (using ``rowBlockDimA=2,`` ``colBlockDimA=3)`` looks like:

   .. math::

       \left[

          \begin{array}{c c c}

           3 & 4 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           2 & 0 & 0 \\
           4 & 5 & 6
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           1 & 2 & 3 \\
           1 & 2 & 0
          \end{array} &

           4 & 0 & 0 \\
           3 & 0 & 1
          \end{array} \\
       \end{array}
      \right]

           1 & 2
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}

           0 & 4 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}

           5 & 6 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} \\

.. py:function:: hipsparseZgebsr2gebsr(handle, dirA, mb, nb, nnzb, descrA, bsrValA, bsrRowPtrA, bsrColIndA, rowBlockDimA, colBlockDimA, descrC, bsrValC, bsrRowPtrC, bsrColIndC, rowBlockDimC, colBlockDimC, buffer)

   This function converts the GEBSR sparse matrix :math:`A` to another GEBSR sparse matrix :math:`C`.

   The conversion uses three steps. First, the user calls ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize`` 
   "hipsparseXgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize()" to determine the size of the required temporary storage buffer.
   The user then allocates this buffer. Secondly, the user then allocates ``mbC+1`` integers for the row
   pointer array for :math:`C` where:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{mbC} &= \text{(m - 1) / rowBlockDimC + 1} \\
      \text{nbC} &= \text{(n - 1) / colBlockDimC + 1}
      \end{align}

   The user then calls hipsparseXgebsr2gebsrNnz() to fill in the row pointer array for :math:`C` ( ``bsrRowPtrC`` ) and
   determine the number of non-zero blocks that will exist in :math:`C`. Finally, the user allocates space for the column
   indices array of :math:`C` to have ``nnzbC`` elements and space for the values array of :math:`C` to have
   ``nnzbC*rowBlockDimC*colBlockDimC`` and then calls ``hipsparseXgebsr2gebsr`` to complete the conversion.

   It could be the case that ``rowBlockDimC`` does not divide evenly into ``m`` or ``colBlockDim`` does not divide evenly
   into ``n.`` In these cases, the GEBSR matrix is expanded in size to fit full GEBSR blocks. For example, if
   the original GEBSR matrix A (using ``rowBlockDimA=2,`` ``colBlockDimA=3)`` looks like:

   .. math::

       \left[
        \begin{array}{c | c}
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           1 & 0 & 0 \\
           3 & 4 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           2 & 0 & 0 \\
           4 & 5 & 6
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           1 & 2 & 3 \\
           1 & 2 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c c}
           4 & 0 & 0 \\
           3 & 0 & 1
          \end{array} \\
       \end{array}
      \right]

   then if the user specifies ``rowBlockDimC=3`` and ``colBlockDimC=2,`` the output GEBSR matrix C would be:

   .. math::

       \left[
        \begin{array}{c | c | c}
          \begin{array}{c c}
           1 & 0 \\
           3 & 4 \\
           1 & 2
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 2 \\
           0 & 4 \\
           3 & 4
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 0 \\
           5 & 6 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} \\
        \hline
          \begin{array}{c c}
           1 & 2 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 3 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} &
          \begin{array}{c c}
           0 & 1 \\
           0 & 0 \\
           0 & 0
          \end{array} \\
       \end{array}
      \right]

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       dirA (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseDirection_t`) -- *IN*:
           the storage format of the blocks, ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_ROW`` or ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_COLUMN`` .

       mb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of block rows of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       nb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of block columns of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       nnzb (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of blocks in the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`A`. The supported matrix type is
           ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` and also any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       bsrValA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzb*rowBlockDimA*colBlockDimA`` containing the values of the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`A`.

       bsrRowPtrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``mb+1`` elements that point to the start of every block row of the
           sparse general BSR matrix :math:`A`.

       bsrColIndA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzb`` elements containing the block column indices of the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`A`.

       rowBlockDimA (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           row size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`A`.

       colBlockDimA (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           column size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`A`.

       descrC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the general BSR sparse matrix :math:`C`. The supported matrix type is
           ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` and any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       bsrValC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzbC*rowBlockDimC*colBlockDimC`` containing the values of the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`C`.

       bsrRowPtrC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``mbC+1`` elements that point to the start of every block row of the
           sparse general BSR matrix :math:`C`.

       bsrColIndC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzbC`` elements containing the block column indices of the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`C`.

       rowBlockDimC (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           row size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`C`.

       colBlockDimC (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           column size of the blocks in the sparse general BSR matrix :math:`C`.

       buffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           buffer allocated by the user. The size is determined by calling ``hipsparseSgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize`` 
           "hipsparseXgebsr2gebsr_bufferSize()".

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``mb,`` ``nb,`` ``nnzb,`` ``rowBlockDimA,`` ``colBlockDimA,``
                 ``rowBlockDimC,`` ``colBlockDimC,`` ``bsrRowPtrA,`` ``bsrColIndA,`` ``bsrValA,`` ``bsrRowPtrC,`` ``bsrColIndC,``
                 ``bsrValC,`` ``descrA,`` ``descrC,`` or ``buffer`` pointer is invalid.

.. py:function:: hipsparseSnnz(handle, dirA, m, n, descrA, A, lda, nnzPerRowColumn, nnzTotalDevHostPtr)

   ``hipsparseXnnz`` computes the number of non-zero elements per row or column and the total
   number of non-zero elements in a dense matrix.

   For example, given the dense matrix:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\
      3 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\
      5 & 0 & 6 & 7
      \end{bmatrix}

   using ``dirA`` == ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_ROW`` results in:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{nnzPerRowColumn} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{nnzTotalDevHostPtr} &= 7
      \end{align}

   while using ``dirA`` == ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_COLUMN`` results in:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{nnzPerRowColumn} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{nnzTotalDevHostPtr} &= 7
      \end{align}

   Note:
       As indicated, ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr`` can point either to host or device memory. This is controlled
       by setting the pointer mode. See ``hipsparseSetPointerMode`` ().

   Note:
       The routine supports asynchronous execution if the pointer mode is set to device.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       dirA (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseDirection_t`) -- *IN*:
           direction that specifies whether to count non-zero elements by ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_ROW`` 
           or by ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_COLUMN`` .

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.``

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``lda,`` ``n).``

       lda (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of dense array ``A.`` Must be at least ``m.``

       nnzPerRowColumn (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of size ``m`` or ``n`` containing the number of non-zero elements per row or column, respectively.

       nnzTotalDevHostPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           total number of non-zero elements in device or host memory.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`: ``handle`` is not initialized.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``descrA,`` ``A,`` ``nnzPerRowColumn,``
                 or ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr`` is nullptr, ``m`` or ``n`` is negative, or ``lda`` is invalid.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseSnnz(hipsparseHandle_t handle, hipsparseDirection_t dirA, int m, int n, const hipsparseMatDescr_t descrA, const float * A, int lda, int * nnzPerRowColumn, int * nnzTotalDevHostPtr)

.. py:function:: hipsparseCnnz(handle, dirA, m, n, descrA, A, lda, nnzPerRowColumn, nnzTotalDevHostPtr)

   ``hipsparseXnnz`` computes the number of non-zero elements per row or column and the total
   number of non-zero elements in a dense matrix.

   For example, given the dense matrix:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\
      3 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\
      5 & 0 & 6 & 7
      \end{bmatrix}

   using ``dirA`` == ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_ROW`` results in:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{nnzPerRowColumn} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{nnzTotalDevHostPtr} &= 7
      \end{align}

   while using ``dirA`` == ``HIPSPARSE_DIRECTION_COLUMN`` results in:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{nnzPerRowColumn} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{nnzTotalDevHostPtr} &= 7
      \end{align}

   Note:
       As indicated, ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr`` can point either to host or device memory. This is controlled
       by setting the pointer mode. See ``hipsparseSetPointerMode`` ().

   Note:
       The routine supports asynchronous execution if the pointer mode is set to device.

       lda (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of dense array ``A.`` Must be at least ``m.``

       nnzPerRowColumn (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of size ``m`` or ``n`` containing the number of non-zero elements per row or column, respectively.

       nnzTotalDevHostPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

.. py:function:: hipsparseSnnz_compress(handle, m, descrA, csrValA, csrRowPtrA, nnzPerRow, nnzC, tol)

   This function is used as the first step in converting a CSR matrix to a compressed CSR matrix.

   Given a sparse CSR matrix and a non-negative tolerance, this function computes how many entries would be left
   in each row of the matrix if elements less than the tolerance were removed. It also computes the total number
   of remaining elements in the matrix.

   Given an input sparse matrix :math:`A` in CSR format, the resulting compressed sparse CSR matrix :math:`C` is
   computed using:

   .. math::

      C(i,j) = A(i, j) \text{  if |A(i, j)| > tol}

   Note:
       In the case of complex matrices, only the magnitude of the real part of ``tol`` is used.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the sparse CSR matrix.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the sparse CSR matrix.

       csrValA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzA`` elements of the sparse CSR matrix.

       csrRowPtrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           uncompressed sparse CSR matrix.

       nnzPerRow (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of length ``m`` containing the number of entries that will be kept per row in
           the final compressed CSR matrix.

       nnzC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           number of elements in the column indices and values arrays of the compressed
           sparse CSR matrix. Can be either host or device pointer.

       tol (:py:obj:`~.float`/:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           the non-negative tolerance used for compression. If ``tol`` is complex, then only the magnitude
           of the real part is used. Entries in the input uncompressed CSR array that are below the tolerance
           are removed in output compressed CSR matrix.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``m,`` ``n,`` ``tol,`` ``csrValA,`` ``csrRowPtrA,`` ``nnzPerRow,`` or ``nnzC``
                 pointer is invalid.

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpruneCsr2csr(handle, m, n, nnzA, descrA, csrValA, csrRowPtrA, csrColIndA, threshold, descrC, csrValC, csrRowPtrC, csrColIndC, buffer)

   Convert and prune a sparse CSR matrix into a sparse CSR matrix.

   This function converts the sparse CSR matrix A into a sparse CSR matrix C by pruning values in A
   that are less than the threshold. All the parameters are assumed to have been preallocated by the user.
   The user first calls ``hipsparseSpruneCsr2csr_bufferSize``  to
   determine the size of the buffer used by ``hipsparseSpruneCsr2csrNnz`` 
   and ``hipsparseXpruneCsr2csr(),`` which the user then allocates. The user then allocates ``csrRowPtrC`` to
   have ``m+1`` elements and then calls hipsparseXpruneCsr2csrNnz(), which fills in the ``csrRowPtrC`` array
   and stores the number of elements that are larger than the pruning ``threshold`` in ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr.``
   The user then calls ``hipsparseXpruneCsr2csr()`` to complete the conversion. This function is executed asynchronously
   with respect to the host and can return control to the application on the host before the entire result is ready.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:

.. py:function:: hipsparseDpruneCsr2csr(handle, m, n, nnzA, descrA, csrValA, csrRowPtrA, csrColIndA, threshold, descrC, csrValC, csrRowPtrC, csrColIndC, buffer)

   Convert and prune a sparse CSR matrix into a sparse CSR matrix.

   This function converts the sparse CSR matrix A into a sparse CSR matrix C by pruning values in A
   that are less than the threshold. All the parameters are assumed to have been preallocated by the user.
   The user first calls ``hipsparseSpruneCsr2csr_bufferSize``  to
   determine the size of the buffer used by ``hipsparseSpruneCsr2csrNnz`` 
   and ``hipsparseXpruneCsr2csr(),`` which the user then allocates. The user then allocates ``csrRowPtrC`` to
   have ``m+1`` elements and then calls hipsparseXpruneCsr2csrNnz(), which fills in the ``csrRowPtrC`` array
   and stores the number of elements that are larger than the pruning ``threshold`` in ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr.``
   The user then calls ``hipsparseXpruneCsr2csr()`` to complete the conversion. This function is executed asynchronously
   with respect to the host and can return control to the application on the host before the entire result is ready.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows in the sparse CSR matrix.

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns in the sparse CSR matrix.

       nnzA (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of non-zeros in the sparse CSR matrix A.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           descriptor of the sparse CSR matrix A. Currently, only
           ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` is supported.

       csrValA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzA`` elements containing the values of the sparse CSR matrix A.

       csrRowPtrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           sparse CSR matrix A.

       csrColIndA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnzA`` elements containing the column indices of the sparse CSR matrix A.

       threshold (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           pointer to the non-negative pruning threshold which can exist in either host or device memory.

       descrC (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           descriptor of the sparse CSR matrix C. Currently, only
           ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` is supported.

           array of ``nnzC`` elements containing the values of the sparse CSR matrix C.

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpruneDense2csr_bufferSize(handle, m, n, A, lda, threshold, descr, csrVal, csrRowPtr, csrColInd, pBufferSizeInBytes)

   ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csr_bufferSize`` computes the the size of the user-allocated temporary storage buffer
   used when converting a dense matrix to a pruned CSR matrix.

   Specifically given an input dense column-ordered matrix A, with leading dimension ``lda,`` where ``lda>=m,``
   the resulting pruned sparse CSR matrix C is computed using:

   .. math::

      |C(i,j)| = A(i, j) \text{  if |A(i, j)| > threshold}

   Deprecated:
       This function is deprecated when using the CUDA backend (CUDA 12.0+) and will be
       removed in CUDA 13.0. This deprecation does not apply to the ROCm backend.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.`` Must be non-negative.

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``lda,`` ``n).``

       lda (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of dense array ``A.`` Must be at least ``m.``

       threshold (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           pointer to the pruning non-negative threshold, which can exist in either host or device memory.

       descr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.`` The supported matrix type is  ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` 
           and any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       csrVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

       csrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           integer array of ``m+1`` elements that contains the start of every row and the end of the last row plus one.

       csrColInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           integer array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) column indices of the non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

       pBufferSizeInBytes (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToUInt64`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           number of bytes of the temporary storage buffer required by
           hipsparseSpruneDense2csrNnz(), hipsparseDpruneDense2csrNnz(),
           hipsparseSpruneDense2csr(), and hipsparseDpruneDense2csr().

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`: ``handle`` is not initialized.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle`` or ``pBufferSizeInBytes`` is nullptr,
                 or ``m`` or ``n`` is negative.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`: an internal error occurred.

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpruneDense2csrNnz(handle, m, n, A, lda, threshold, descr, csrRowPtr, nnzTotalDevHostPtr, buffer)

   ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csrNnz`` computes the number of non-zero elements per row and the total
   number of non-zero elements in a dense matrix after the elements less than the (non-negative) threshold are
   pruned from the matrix.

   Given an input dense column ordered matrix ``A,`` with leading dimension ``lda`` where ``lda>=m,``
   the resulting pruned sparse CSR matrix :math:`C` is computed using:

   .. math::

      |C(i,j)| = A(i, j) \text{  if |A(i, j)| > threshold}

   First, the user must determine the size of the required temporary buffer using the routine
   ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csr_bufferSize``  and then allocate it. Next,
   the user allocates ``csrRowPtr`` with size ``m+1.`` Then the function passes both the temporary storage buffer and
   ``csrRowPtr`` to ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csrNnz`` to determine the total number of non-zeros that
   will exist in the sparse CSR matrix C (after pruning has been performed on ``A`` ) as well as fill the output CSR
   row pointer array ``csrRowPtr.``

   For example, given the dense matrix:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      6 & 2 & 3 & 7 \\
      5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
      5 & 4 & 8 & 1
      \end{bmatrix}

   and the ``threshold`` value 5, the resulting matrix after pruning is:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      6 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\
      0 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
      0 & 0 & 8 & 0
      \end{bmatrix}

   and the corresponding row pointer array and non-zero count:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{csrRowPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 5 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{nnzTotalDevHostPtr} &= 6
      \end{align}

   Note:
       The routine supports asynchronous execution if the pointer mode is set to device.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.``

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.``

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``lda,`` ``n).``

       lda (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of the dense array ``A.``

       threshold (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           pointer to the pruning non-negative threshold, which can exist in either host or device memory.

       descr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.``

       csrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           integer array of ``m+1`` elements that contains the start of every row and the end of the last row plus one.

       nnzTotalDevHostPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           total number of non-zero elements in device or host memory.

       buffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           buffer allocated by the user whose size is determined by calling
           ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csr_bufferSize``  or
           ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csr_bufferSizeExt`` .

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``m,`` ``n,`` ``lda,`` ``A,`` ``threshold,`` ``descr,`` ``csrRowPtr,``
                 ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr,`` or ``buffer`` pointer is invalid.

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpruneDense2csr(handle, m, n, A, lda, threshold, descr, csrVal, csrRowPtr, csrColInd, buffer)

   ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csr`` converts the matrix ``A`` in dense format into a sparse matrix in CSR format,
   while pruning values that are less than the (non-negative) threshold. All the parameters are assumed
   to have been pre-allocated by the user.

   Given an input dense column ordered matrix ``A,`` with leading dimension ``lda,`` where ``lda>=m,``
   the resulting pruned sparse CSR matrix C is computed using:

   .. math::

      |C(i,j)| = A(i, j) \text{  if |A(i, j)| > threshold}

   The user first calls ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csr_bufferSize``  to
   determine the size of the required user-allocated temporary storage buffer. The user then allocates this
   buffer. Next, the user allocates ``csrRowPtr`` to have ``m+1`` elements and then calls
   ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrNnz`` , which fills in the ``csrRowPtr`` array
   and stores the number of elements that are larger than the pruning ``threshold`` in ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr.``
   The user then allocates ``csrColInd`` and ``csrVal`` to have size ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr`` and completes the
   conversion by calling ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csr().``

   For example, performing these steps with the dense input matrix ``A`` :

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      6 & 2 & 3 & 7 \\
      5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
      5 & 4 & 8 & 1
      \end{bmatrix}

   and the ``threshold`` value 5, results in the pruned matrix C:

   .. math::

      \begin{bmatrix}
      6 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\
      0 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
      0 & 0 & 8 & 0
      \end{bmatrix}

   and corresponding CSR row, column, and values arrays:

   .. math::

      \begin{align}
      \text{csrRowPtr} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 5 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{csrColInd} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \text{csrVal} &= \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 7 & 6 & 7 & 8 & 8 \end{bmatrix} \\
      \end{align}

   Note:
       The routine ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csr()`` is executed asynchronously with respect to the host and can
       return control to the application on the host before the entire result is ready.

           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.``

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``lda,`` ``n).``

           leading dimension of dense array ``A.``

           pointer to the non-negative pruning threshold, which can exist in either host or device memory.

       descr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.`` The supported matrix type is  ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` 
           and any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       csrVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

           integer array of ``m+1`` elements that contains the start of every row and the end of the last row plus one.

           integer array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) column indices of the non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize(handle, m, n, A, lda, percentage, descr, csrVal, csrRowPtr, csrColInd, info, pBufferSizeInBytes)

   ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize`` functions convert the size of the user-allocated temporary
   storage buffer used when converting a dense matrix to a pruned CSR matrix where the pruning is done
   based on a ``percentage.``

   When converting and pruning a dense matrix ``A`` to a CSR matrix by percentage, the
   following steps are performed. First, the user calls
   ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize,`` which determines the size of the
   temporary storage buffer. After this is determined, this buffer must be allocated by the user.
   Next, the user allocates the ``csrRowPtr`` array to have ``m+1`` elements and calls
   ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrNnzByPercentage`` .
   Finally, the user finishes the conversion by allocating the ``csrColInd`` and ``csrVal`` arrays
   (whose size is determined by the value at ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr)`` and calling
   ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrByPercentage`` .

   The pruning by ``percentage`` works by first sorting the absolute values of the dense
   matrix ``A.`` Users can then determine a position in this sorted array by

   .. math::

      pos = ceil(m \cdot n \cdot (percentage/100)) - 1 \\
      pos = \min(pos, m \cdot n-1) \\
      pos = \max(pos, 0) \\
      threshold = sorted_A[pos]

   Note:
       This function is executed asynchronously with respect to the host and can return control to the
       application on the host before the entire result is ready.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.``

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:

.. py:function:: hipsparseDpruneDense2csrByPercentage(handle, m, n, A, lda, percentage, descr, csrVal, csrRowPtr, csrColInd, info, buffer)

   This function computes the number of non-zero elements per row and the total number of
   non-zero elements in a dense matrix when converting and pruning by ``percentage`` a dense
   matrix to a CSR matrix.

   When converting and pruning a dense matrix ``A`` to a CSR matrix by ``percentage,`` the
   following steps are performed. First, the user calls ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize`` 
   "hipsparseXpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize()", which determines the size of the
   temporary storage buffer. After this is determined, this buffer must be allocated by the user.
   Next, the user allocates the ``csrRowPtr`` array to have ``m+1`` elements and calls
   ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrNnzByPercentage`` . Finally, the
   user finishes the conversion by allocating the ``csrColInd`` and ``csrVal`` arrays (which have a size
   determined by the value at ``nnzTotalDevHostPtr)`` and calling ``hipsparseXpruneDense2csrByPercentage.``

   The pruning by ``percentage`` works by first sorting the absolute values of the dense
   matrix ``A.`` Users can then determine a position in this sorted array by

   .. math::

      pos = ceil(m \ cdot n \cdot (percentage/100)) - 1 \\
      pos = \min(pos, m \cdot n-1) \\
      pos = \max(pos, 0) \\
      threshold = sorted_A[pos]

   Note:
       This routine support asynchronous execution if the pointer mode is set to device.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of the dense matrix ``A.``

       n (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of columns of the dense matrix ``A.``

       A (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of dimensions (``lda,`` ``n).``

       lda (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           leading dimension of dense array ``A.``

       percentage (:py:obj:`~.float`/:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           ``percentage>=0`` and ``percentage<=100.``

       descr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           the descriptor of the dense matrix ``A.`` The supported matrix type is  ``HIPSPARSE_MATRIX_TYPE_GENERAL`` and
           any valid value of the ``hipsparseIndexBase_t`` .

       csrVal (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

       csrRowPtr (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           integer array of ``m+1`` elements that contains the start of every row and the end of the last row plus one.

       csrColInd (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           integer array of nnz ( = ``csrRowPtr[m]`` - ``csrRowPtr[0]`` ) column indices of the non-zero elements of matrix ``A.``

       info (:py:obj:`~.pruneInfo`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           prune  information structure

       buffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user. The size is returned by
           ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSize``  or
           ``hipsparseSpruneDense2csrByPercentage_bufferSizeExt`` .

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``m,`` ``n,`` ``lda,`` ``percentage,`` ``A,`` ``descr,`` ``info,`` ``csrVal,``
                 ``csrRowPtr,`` ``csrColInd,`` or ``buffer`` pointer is invalid.

.. py:function:: hipsparseScsrcolor(handle, m, nnz, descrA, csrValA, csrRowPtrA, csrColIndA, fractionToColor, ncolors, coloring, reordering, info)

   Coloring of the adjacency graph of the matrix :math:`A` stored in the CSR format.

   ``hipsparseXcsrcolor`` performs the coloring of the undirected graph represented by the (symmetric) sparsity
   pattern of the matrix :math:`A` stored in CSR format. Graph coloring is a way of coloring the nodes of a graph
   such that no two adjacent nodes are of the same color. The ``fractionToColor`` is a parameter to only color
   a given percentage of the graph nodes. The remaining uncolored nodes receive distinct new colors. The optional
   ``reordering`` array is a permutation array that groups unknowns of the same color. The matrix :math:`A`
   must be stored as a general matrix with a symmetric sparsity pattern, and if the matrix :math:`A` is non-symmetric,
   then the user is responsible to provide the symmetric part :math:`\frac{A+A^T}{2}`.

   Deprecated:
       This function is deprecated when using the CUDA backend (CUDA 12.0+) and will be
       removed in CUDA 13.0. This deprecation does not apply to the ROCm backend.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       m (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of rows of sparse matrix :math:`A`. Must be non-negative.

       nnz (:py:obj:`~.int`) -- *IN*:
           number of non-zero entries of sparse matrix :math:`A`. Must be non-negative.

       descrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           sparse matrix descriptor.

       csrValA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements of the sparse CSR matrix.

       csrRowPtrA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``m+1`` elements that point to the start of every row of the
           sparse CSR matrix.

       csrColIndA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           array of ``nnz`` elements containing the column indices of the sparse
           CSR matrix.

       fractionToColor (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           fraction of nodes to be colored, which should be in the interval :math:`[0.0,1.0]`. For example, :math:`0.8` implies that
           :math:`80` percent of nodes will be colored.

       ncolors (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           resulting number of distinct colors.

       coloring (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           resulting mapping of colors.

       reordering (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToInt`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           optional resulting reordering permutation if ``reordering`` is a non-null pointer.

       info (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *INOUT*:
           structure that holds the information collected during the coloring algorithm.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`: ``handle`` is not initialized.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``descrA,`` ``fractionToColor,``
                 ``ncolors,`` ``coloring,`` or ``info`` is nullptr, ``m`` or ``nnz`` is negative, or
                 ``csrValA,`` ``csrRowPtrA,`` or ``csrColIndA`` is nullptr when ``nnz`` is greater than zero.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseScsrcolor(hipsparseHandle_t handle, int m, int nnz, const hipsparseMatDescr_t descrA, const float * csrValA, const int * csrRowPtrA, const int * csrColIndA, const float * fractionToColor, int * ncolors, int * coloring, int * reordering, hipsparseColorInfo_t info)

.. py:function:: hipsparseAxpby(handle, alpha, vecX, beta, vecY)

   Scale a sparse vector and add it to a scaled dense vector.

   ``hipsparseAxpby`` multiplies the sparse vector :math:`x` with scalar :math:`\alpha` and
   adds the result to the dense vector :math:`y` that is multiplied with scalar
   :math:`\beta`, such that

   .. math::

      y := \alpha \cdot x + \beta \cdot y

   .. code-block::

      for(i = 0; i < size; ++i)
      {
          y[i] = beta * y[i]
      }
      for(i = 0; i < nnz; ++i)
      {
          y[xInd[i]] += alpha * xVal[i]
      }

   Par:
       <table>
       <caption id="axpby_uniform">Uniform Precisions</caption>
       <tr><th>X / Y / compute_type
       <tr><td>HIP_R_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_R_64F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_64F
       </table>

   Par:
       <table>
       <caption id="axpby_mixed">Mixed Precisions</caption>
       <tr><th>X / Y      <th>compute_type
       <tr><td>HIP_R_16F  <td>HIP_R_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_R_16BF <td>HIP_R_32F
       </table>

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       alpha (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           scalar :math:`\alpha`.

       vecX (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           sparse vector descriptor.

       beta (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           scalar :math:`\beta`.

       vecY (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *INOUT*:
           dense vector descriptor.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`: ``handle`` is not initialized.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``alpha,`` ``vecX,`` ``beta,`` or ``vecY`` is nullptr,
                 or the vector sizes or data types are incompatible.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseAxpby(hipsparseHandle_t handle, const void * alpha, hipsparseConstSpVecDescr_t vecX, const void * beta, hipsparseDnVecDescr_t vecY)


.. py:function:: hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize(handle, matA, matB, alg, pBufferSizeInBytes)

   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize`` computes the required user-allocated buffer size needed when converting
   a dense matrix to a sparse matrix.

   This routine currently accepts the sparse matrix descriptor ``matB`` in CSR,
   CSC, or COO format. This routine is used to determine the size of the buffer
   needed in ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis`` and ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert`` .

   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize`` supports different data types for the dense and sparse matrices. See
   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert`` for a complete listing of all the data types available.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       matA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           dense matrix descriptor.

       matB (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseSpMatDescr_st`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           sparse matrix descriptor.

       alg (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseDenseToSparseAlg_t`) -- *IN*:
           algorithm for the dense to sparse computation.

       pBufferSizeInBytes (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.PointerToUInt64`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           number of bytes of the temporary storage buffer.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``matA,`` ``matB,`` or ``pBufferSizeInBytes``
                 pointer is invalid.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize(hipsparseHandle_t handle, hipsparseConstDnMatDescr_t matA, hipsparseSpMatDescr_t matB, hipsparseDenseToSparseAlg_t alg, size_t * pBufferSizeInBytes)


.. py:function:: hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis(handle, matA, matB, alg, externalBuffer)

   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis`` performs analysis that is later used in ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert`` when
   converting a dense matrix to sparse matrix.

   This routine currently accepts the sparse matrix descriptor ``matB`` in CSR,
   CSC, or COO format. This routine takes a user-allocated buffer with a size that must first be computed
   using ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize`` .

   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis`` supports different data types for the dense and sparse matrices. See
   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert`` for a complete listing of all the data types available.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       matA (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           dense matrix descriptor.

       matB (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseSpMatDescr_st`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           sparse matrix descriptor.

       alg (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseDenseToSparseAlg_t`) -- *IN*:
           algorithm for the dense to sparse computation.

       externalBuffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *OUT*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user.

   Returns:
       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

       * :py:obj:`~.hipsparseStatus_t`: One of:
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_SUCCESS`: the operation completed successfully.
               - :py:obj:`~.HIPSPARSE_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`: ``handle,`` ``matA,`` ``matB,`` or ``externalBuffer``
                 pointer is invalid.

   .. rubric:: C signature

   .. code-block:: c

       hipsparseStatus_t hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis(hipsparseHandle_t handle, hipsparseConstDnMatDescr_t matA, hipsparseSpMatDescr_t matB, hipsparseDenseToSparseAlg_t alg, void * externalBuffer)


.. py:function:: hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert(handle, matA, matB, alg, externalBuffer)

   Dense matrix to sparse matrix conversion.

   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_convert`` converts a dense matrix to a sparse matrix. This routine currently accepts
   the sparse matrix descriptor ``matB`` in CSR, CSC, or COO format. This routine requires a user-allocated buffer
   with a size that must first be determined by calling ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize`` .

   The conversion of a dense matrix into a sparse one involves three steps. First, the user creates the dense and
   sparse matrix descriptors. Because the number of non-zeros that will exist in the sparse matrix is not known beforehand,
   when creating the sparse matrix descriptor, the user simply sets the arrays to ``NULL`` and the non-zero count to zero.
   For example, in the case of a CSR sparse matrix, this would look like:

   .. code-block::

      hipsparseCreateCsr(&matB,
                         m,
                         n,
                         0,
                         dcsrRowPtrB, // This array can be allocated as its size (i.e. m + 1) is known
                         NULL,        // Column indices array size is not yet known, pass NULL for now
                         NULL,        // Values array size is not yet known, pass NULL for now
                         rowIdxTypeB,
                         colIdxTypeB,
                         idxBaseB,
                         dataTypeB);

   In the case of a COO sparse matrix, this would look like:

   .. code-block::

      hipsparseCreateCoo(&matB,
                         m,
                         n,
                         0,
                         NULL,  // Row indices array size is not yet known, pass NULL for now
                         NULL,  // Column indices array size is not yet known, pass NULL for now
                         NULL,  // Values array size is not yet known, pass NULL for now
                         rowIdxTypeB,
                         colIdxTypeB,
                         idxBaseB,
                         dataTypeB);

   After the descriptors have been created, the user calls ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_bufferSize`` . This routine will
   determine the size of the required temporary storage buffer. The user then allocates this buffer and passes it to
   ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis`` , which will perform analysis on the dense matrix to determine the number
   of non-zeros that will exist in the sparse matrix. After the ``hipsparseDenseToSparse_analysis`` routine has been
   called, the non-zero count is stored in the sparse matrix descriptor ``matB.`` To allocate the remaining sparse
   matrix arrays, query the sparse matrix descriptor ``matB`` for this non-zero count:

   .. code-block::

      // Grab the non-zero count from the B matrix decriptor
      int64_t rows;
      int64_t cols;
      int64_t nnz;
      hipsparseSpMatGetSize(matB, &rows, &cols, &nnz);

.. py:function:: hipsparseRot(handle, c_coeff, s_coeff, vecX, vecY)

   Apply the Givens rotation to a dense and a sparse vector.

   ``hipsparseRot`` applies the Givens rotation matrix :math:`G` to the sparse vector
   :math:`x` and the dense vector :math:`y`, where

   .. math::

      G = \begin{pmatrix} c & s \\ -s & c \end{pmatrix}

   .. code-block::

      for(i = 0; i < nnz; ++i)
      {
          x_tmp = x_val[i];
          y_tmp = y[x_ind[i]];

          x_val[i]    = c * x_tmp + s * y_tmp;
          y[x_ind[i]] = c * y_tmp - s * x_tmp;
      }

.. py:function:: hipsparseSDDMM(handle, opA, opB, alpha, A, B, beta, C, computeType, alg, tempBuffer)

   Sampled dense-dense matrix multiplication.

   ``hipsparseSDDMM`` multiplies the scalar :math:`\alpha` with the dense
   :math:`m \times k` matrix :math:`op(A)`, the dense :math:`k \times n` matrix :math:`op(B)`, filtered by the sparsity pattern
   of the :math:`m \times n` sparse matrix :math:`C`, and adds the result to :math:`C` scaled by
   :math:`\beta`. The final result is stored in the sparse :math:`m \times n` matrix :math:`C`,
   such that

   .. math::

      C := \alpha ( op(A) \cdot op(B) ) \circ spy(C) + \beta C,

   with

   .. math::

      op(A) = \left*    \begin{array}{ll}
          A,   & \text{if op(A) == HIPSPARSE_OPERATION_NON_TRANSPOSE} \\
          A^T, & \text{if op(A) == HIPSPARSE_OPERATION_TRANSPOSE} \\
      \end{array}
      \right.

   ,

   .. math::

      op(B) = \left*    \begin{array}{ll}
          B,   & \text{if op(B) == HIPSPARSE_OPERATION_NON_TRANSPOSE} \\
          B^T, & \text{if op(B) == HIPSPARSE_OPERATION_TRANSPOSE} \\
      \end{array}
      \right.

   and

   .. math::

      spy(C)_{ij} = \left*    \begin{array}{ll}
          1, & \text{ if C_{ij} != 0} \\
          0, & \text{ otherwise} \\
      \end{array}
      \right.

       <tr><td>HIP_R_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_R_64F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_64F
       </table>

   Par:

       <tr><td>HIP_R_16BF <td>HIP_R_16BF <td>HIP_R_32F
       </table>

.. py:function:: hipsparseSparseToDense(handle, matA, matB, alg, externalBuffer)

   Sparse matrix to dense matrix conversion

   ``hipsparseSparseToDense`` converts a sparse matrix to a dense matrix. This routine accepts
   the sparse matrix descriptor ``matA`` in CSR, CSC, or COO format. It takes a user-allocated buffer
   with a size that must first be computed by calling ``hipsparseSparseToDense_bufferSize`` .

   The conversion of a sparse matrix into a dense one involves two steps. First, the user creates the sparse and
   dense matrix descriptors and calls ``hipsparseSparseToDense_bufferSize`` to determine the size of the required
   temporary storage buffer. The user then allocates this buffer and passes it to ``hipsparseSparseToDense`` 
   to complete the conversion. After the conversion is complete, the user is free to deallocate the storage
   buffer. See the full example below for details.

   ``hipsparseSparseToDense`` supports the following uniform precision data types for the sparse and dense matrices :math:`A`
   and :math:`B`:

   Par:

       <tr><td>HIP_R_16F
       <tr><td>HIP_R_16BF
       <tr><td>HIP_R_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_R_64F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_32F
       <tr><td>HIP_C_64F
       </table>

   Note:
       Currently only the sparse matrix formats CSR, CSC, and COO are supported when converting a sparse matrix to a dense matrix.

   Args:
       handle (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           handle to the hipSPARSE library context queue.

       matA (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseSpMatDescr_st`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           sparse matrix descriptor.

       matB (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           dense matrix descriptor.

       alg (:py:obj:`~.hipsparseSparseToDenseAlg_t`) -- *IN*:
           algorithm for the sparse to dense computation.

       externalBuffer (:py:obj:`~.rocm.bindings.util.types.Pointer`/:py:obj:`~.object`) -- *IN*:
           temporary storage buffer allocated by the user.

       A :py:obj:`~.tuple` of size 1 that contains (in that order):

.. py:function:: hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation(handle, opA, opB, alpha, matA, matB, beta, matC, computeType, alg, spgemmDescr, bufferSize1, externalBuffer1)

   Work estimation step of the sparse matrix sparse matrix product:

   .. math::

      C' := \alpha \cdot op(A) \cdot op(B) + \beta \cdot C,

   ``hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation`` is called twice. First, call it to compute the size of the first required user-allocated
   buffer. After this buffer size is determined, allocate the buffer and call ``hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation``
   a second time with the newly allocated buffer passed in. This second call inspects the matrices :math:`A` and :math:`B` to
   determine the number of intermediate products that will result from multiplying :math:`A` and :math:`B` together.

   ``hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation`` supports multiple combinations of data types and compute types. See ``hipsparseSpGEMM_copy`` 
   for a complete listing of all the data type and compute type combinations available.

   Par:

   .. code-block::

      void*  dBuffer1  = NULL;
      size_t bufferSize1 = 0;

      hipsparseSpGEMMDescr_t spgemmDesc;
      hipsparseSpGEMM_createDescr(&spgemmDesc);

      size_t bufferSize1 = 0;
      hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation(handle, opA, opB,
                                    &alpha, matA, matB, &beta, matC,
                                    computeType, HIPSPARSE_SPGEMM_DEFAULT,
                                    spgemmDesc, &bufferSize1, NULL);
      hipMalloc((void**) &dBuffer1, bufferSize1);

      // Determine number of intermediate product when computing A * B
      hipsparseSpGEMM_workEstimation(handle, opA, opB,
                                      &alpha, matA, matB, &beta, matC,
                                      computeType, HIPSPARSE_SPGEMM_DEFAULT,
                                      spgemmDesc, &bufferSize1, dBuffer1);
